**Finding submitted: MISSING (INSURANCE)**

**What I checked**
- Full-document searches for "insurance", "fidelity bond", "errors and omissions" — only unrelated hits (billed insurance premiums in the Servicing Procedures, FDIC deposit insurance in the definitions).
- Article VI (Servicer and Marketing Agent) in full: representations (6.1), liability (6.2), indemnities (6.3), delegation/contracting (6.4), Reg AB compliance (6.6–6.7) — no coverage covenant.
- Article X Miscellaneous in full: runs through Section 10.13; no insurance section.
- Confirmed the exposure driver: Cellco holds/processes Obligor **Personally Identifiable Information** and may subcontract its obligations under Section 6.4.

**Why it's a deviation rather than acceptable**
No insurance at all for a counterparty that processes personal data is the playbook's walk-away scenario. The Section 6.3 indemnity is not a substitute — it is capped to willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, so ordinary-negligence data incidents are uncovered and unbacked by any carrier.

**Redline (validated ok:true)**
New **Section 10.14 Insurance** inserted at the end of Article X (after p0439), at the preferred position: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M while Obligor PII is held or processed, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request to the Issuer, Depositor and Indenture Trustee. Drafted to bind both the Servicer and the Marketing Agent, since both are Cellco capacities under this Agreement. The comment offers the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) if the Servicer pushes back on limits.
